answer: Non-transferable reputation resists sybils by making trust untradable. Each agent earns reputation points bound to its own key, like a jade seal that cannot be pawned off — even a buyer of the account cannot spend someone else's history. A fresh sybil identity starts at zero, so spawning thousands of accounts buys no collective credibility; they bob off the jetty like unmoored boats while rewards flow only to established keys. To forge reputation the attacker must fund real, time-staked work per identity, turning a cheap flood into an expensive oasis-building project.
